message.content:
You are running a design finish review. You did not build this artifact and must not assume the builder's framing was right. Be specific and hard to please; vague praise is worthless.

ORIGINAL REQUEST (from the user, verbatim): "take 1 slide of the 5 we just made and using /impeccable create a completely new design." Follow-up context: the five existing decks all share one composition and the user said "all the slides look good but they look the same." The brief passed to the design skill added: redesign slide 3 ("the insight") of the Data to Decision deck; the current look is a split field with a forest claim panel on the left 38%, a bone evidence field right, gold hairline seam, and a horizontal "noise band" visual; the user wants "a genuinely different composition and a different way of drawing the typical-error band — not a re-skin"; output is a 16:9 PowerPoint slide built with pptxgenjs.

FIXED CONSTRAINTS (not negotiable, from the department's design system):
- Palette: forest #0B2A1F ground, Baylor green #154734, mid green #1E6349, Baylor gold #FFB81C (DARK grounds only — 1.7:1 on light), antique gold #9A8033 for light-ground gold/hairlines, pale mint #AFD2C0 secondary text on dark (~9:1), mint surface #E4F0E9, bone #F4F2EC light ground, gray-green #4E5150 light grounds only.
- Type: DIN Pro, DIN Pro Light, DIN Pro Cond, DIN Pro Cond Medium; the "Baylor Bears Font" display face is allowed exactly once per deck and only on slide 1, so it must NOT appear here.
- Contrast floor is 3.0:1 for text against its containing shape.
- Gold accent count on one slide is capped at 2 objects.

PRODUCT TRUTH:
- This is a 5-minute staff-meeting slide for cross-functional Baylor Athletics Health & Wellness staff (S&C, athletic medicine, sport science, nutrition, mental health) presented to as peers. Several know their discipline better than the presenter. Anything overstated gets caught by name in the room. Projector, mixed lighting, people half-turned in chairs.
- Every number must trace to a source. The 3.0% coefficient of variation and ICC 0.96 come from Rebelo et al., Sports Medicine 2026. The "±1 SD" is described in that paper as one example of a sensitive setting, not a standard. The −2.0% and −6.0% readings are ILLUSTRATIVE and the slide must say so.
- Doctrine: establish the noise floor before claiming a change is meaningful; decoration must not imply more certainty than the evidence supports.

THE DIRECTION CONTRACT the build committed to (judge the render against this):
- THESIS: measurement error is a manufacturing tolerance, so draw it the way a shop drawing does. Refuses the category default — a shaded band with the explanation typeset inside it.
- OWN-WORLD: a blueprint. Deep forest sheet, mint hairlines at drafting weight, 45° section hatch in mid green, condensed all-caps annotation tracked wide, a ruled notes column down the left and a title block across the foot. Baylor gold spent once, on the tolerance dimension. Recognisable with every word removed.
- STORY: the room sees a dimensioned zone before it sees a claim; understands that a reading inside it is not an observation; and leaves knowing the threshold is drawn dashed because a person sets it.
- FIRST VIEWPORT: notes column left, gold tolerance dimension over a hatched zone centred on the baseline, two readings called out below the axis, general notes ruled across the foot, title block carrying the claim bottom-left.

WHAT TO INSPECT:
1. The render proof (read this image): /Users/kristinarash/DEV/Education_Content_Agent/decks-out/design-studies/Data_to_Decision_S3_ToleranceDrawing_proof.png — a 16:9 slide letterboxed into a square canvas; the dark grey bands top and bottom are padding, not part of the slide.
2. The source: /Users/kristinarash/DEV/Education_Content_Agent/.claude/worktrees/design-variants/decks/build-blueprint.js
3. The incumbent look it must differ from: /Users/kristinarash/DEV/Education_Content_Agent/.claude/worktrees/design-variants/decks/variants/split-field.js and the narrative source /Users/kristinarash/DEV/Education_Content_Agent/.claude/worktrees/design-variants/decks/data-to-decision.js (the `insight` block is the content this slide carries — check nothing meaningful was dropped or altered).
4. The quality floor: /Users/kristinarash/.claude/skills/impeccable/reference/craft-floor.md — read it and apply it.

Note: the proof is rendered by a small in-house SVG renderer, so text metrics are approximate. Judge composition, hierarchy, colour, spacing, and legibility-at-projector-distance; do NOT report tiny kerning or exact line-break differences as defects.

RETURN exactly these five sections, nothing else:
1. VERDICT — one word: pass, pass-with-fixes, or rebuild.
2. CONTRACT AUDIT — for each of THESIS / OWN-WORLD / STORY / FIRST VIEWPORT, does the render keep it? Say where it does not.
3. MATERIAL FINDINGS — numbered, most severe first. Each: what is wrong, where (element and approximate coordinates or the source line), why it matters to THIS room, and the specific fix. Only things that would change what a viewer understands or whether they can read it. If you find none, say so plainly.
4. TRUTH CHECK — any claim, number, or visual that overstates the evidence, or any illustrative figure not labelled as illustrative.
5. WHAT NOT TO CHANGE — the parts that are working, so a fix pass does not sand them off.
<context_window_protection>
  <priority_instructions>
    Every byte a tool returns enters your conversation memory and costs reasoning capacity for the rest of the session. The context-mode tools let you do the work in a sandbox and surface only the derived answer — the raw bytes stay out. Think-in-Code: program the analysis, do not compute it by reading raw data into your conversation.
  </priority_instructions>

  <deferred_tool_bootstrap>
    The context-mode tools below may be DEFERRED in your harness — their schemas are not loaded yet, so calling them directly fails (e.g. "tool not found" / InputValidationError). Load them ONCE before your first ctx_* call:
    ToolSearch(query: "select:mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_batch_execute,mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_search,mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute,mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute_file,mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_fetch_and_index")
    After that they are callable. If any ctx_* call fails as not-found, ToolSearch it and retry — do NOT fall back to Bash/Read just because the schema was not loaded yet.
  </deferred_tool_bootstrap>

  <tool_selection_hierarchy>
    0. MEMORY: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_search(sort: "timeline")
       - On resume or compaction, query prior decisions, errors, plans, user prompts before asking the user — auto-captured session memory is searchable.
    1. GATHER: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_batch_execute(commands, queries)
       - Primary research tool. Runs commands in parallel, auto-indexes each output, and (when queries are passed) returns matching sections in the same round trip — no follow-up search call.
       - Each command: {label: "section header", command: "shell command"}; the label becomes the FTS5 chunk title — descriptive labels improve search.
    2. FOLLOW-UP: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_search(queries: ["q1", "q2", ...])
       - Multiple related questions about anything already indexed (your captures + session memory). Batch every question in one array; the ranking pipeline runs per-query and the round-trip cost is paid once.
    3. PROCESSING: mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute(language, code) | mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute_file(path, language, code)
       - Derive answers FROM data: filter, count, aggregate, parse, transform. Only what you console.log() enters your conversation; the raw bytes stay in the sandbox.
  </tool_selection_hierarchy>

  <when_not_to_use>
    - You intend to PROCESS the output (filter, count, parse, aggregate) → use mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_batch_execute or mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute. Bash stays correct when you intend to OBSERVE a short fixed output (git status on a clean tree, whoami, pwd) or when you are mutating state (git, mkdir, rm, mv, navigation).
    - You want to analyze, summarize, or extract from a file → use mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute_file. Read stays correct when you intend to Edit the file (Edit needs the exact bytes in your conversation to match against).
    - WebFetch → use mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_fetch_and_index; full network access, results indexed for mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_search, raw page bytes never enter your conversation.
    - mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute and mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute_file for file writes → these run code in a subprocess and discard the sandbox FS; they are for analysis, processing, and computation only.
  </when_not_to_use>

  <file_writing_policy>
    File writes use the native Write or Edit tool — mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute, mcp__plugin_context-mode_context-mode__ctx_execute_file, and Bash subprocesses do not persist edits to the host filesystem.
    Applies to all file types: code, configs, plans, specs, YAML, JSON, markdown.
  </file_writing_policy>

  <output_constraints>
    <artifact_policy>
      Write artifacts (code, configs, PRDs) to files. Return only: file path + 1-line description.
    </artifact_policy>
  </output_constraints>
  <session_continuity>
    Skills, roles, and decisions captured earlier in this session are a memory aid, not a standing order. Treat them as context that may help — the user's most recent message always takes precedence. If a captured directive conflicts with what the user now asks, follow the user; a past phrase does not bind you.
  </session_continuity>

</context_window_protection>

# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in the batched inspection rounds, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.

content.text:
VERDICT

pass-with-fixes. The composition and own-world are sound; every finding below is a fix inside the existing skeleton (notes column / dimensioned zone / readings / general notes / title block), not a reason to start over.

CONTRACT AUDIT

**THESIS — kept.** It genuinely refuses the category default. There is no shaded band with a paragraph typeset inside it; the explanation is displaced to a ruled column and to leader callouts, and the tolerance is read as a dimension rather than as a fill. The one soft spot: the shop-drawing genre wants dense small annotation, and the use scene is a projector. The build sided with the genre. That tension is the root of finding 1.

**OWN-WORLD — kept, and this is the strongest part of the render.** Strip every word and you still have a shop drawing: sheet frame, ruled column, hatched zone with extension lines, dimension with arrowheads, ticked datum axis, dogleg leaders, title-block grid. Nothing in the incumbent's split-field world resembles it. It is not a re-skin.

**STORY — beats 1 and 2 kept, beat 3 fails.** The room does see a dimensioned zone before a claim (beat 1), and Reading A inside it captioned "Inside the floor. Nothing has been observed yet." carries beat 2. Beat 3 — "leaves knowing the threshold is drawn dashed because a person sets it" — hangs entirely on a 6.5pt `ADJ.` (`build-blueprint.js`, the threshold loop) plus a notes-column heading four inches away. `ADJ.` is drafting jargon this room will not decode, at a size it cannot read. The single most important idea on the slide has the smallest type on the sheet.

**FIRST VIEWPORT — kept literally.** Notes column left, gold dimension over a hatched zone centred on the baseline (verified: zone 4.70–7.40in, centre 6.05in = the zero datum), two readings called out below the axis, general notes ruled across the foot, title block bottom-left. All present as specified.

MATERIAL FINDINGS

**1. Type scale sits below the projection floor across the entire sheet, and the hierarchy is inverted.** Annotation runs 6.5–8pt (`adj.` 6.5, general notes 7, source 7, axis labels 7.5, notes-column body 7.5, reading body 8, header 8). At 7pt on a 5.625in-tall slide that is 1.7% of slide height; projected text needs roughly 2.5–3% to survive a mixed-lit room with people half-turned in chairs. Meanwhile the largest type on the slide is `3 / 5` at 24pt (title block, x 7.86in) and the second largest is the deck topic at 12pt — a page number and a subject line outrank every idea on the sheet. The claim itself is 20pt.

Why it matters here: this is a 5-minute slide for peers who will be reading at distance. Anything under ~11pt is decoration they will not consume, which means Notes 1–3 — including the illustrative disclaimer and the ±1 SD caveat — are effectively invisible to the room and only exist for whoever gets the file.

Fix, and this is the important part: **cut copy, then rescale — scaling alone will break the sheet.** The notes column is 1.94in wide and cannot hold its current words at 11–12pt. Concretely: drop `3 / 5` to ~13pt and the subject to ~10pt; raise the claim to ~26pt; raise reading bodies and the notes column to ~11pt and cut each to one or two lines; raise general notes to ~10pt and cut Note 2 to its first and last sentence (the full argument is already in the speaker notes). The hollow lower-right of the drawing area (roughly x 7.6–9.5in, y 3.2–3.9in) can absorb the rewrapped Reading A block.

**2. Reading A's leader routes under "0 · BASELINE" and terminates in positive territory.** `reading(-2, { noteX: 6.10 })` — the marker is at 5.15in, the dogleg runs right along y=3.18in and drops at x=6.10in, which is 0.05in to the *right* of the zero datum at 6.05in. The horizontal segment passes directly beneath the `0 · BASELINE` label (y 2.99–3.15in). Confirmed in the crop: the line visually connects "0 · BASELINE" to "READING A −2.0%", and a negative reading is annotated on the positive side of zero. In a room that reads numbers carefully this is a misread waiting to be named. Fix: route Reading A's leader *left* to a note origin at ~x 4.75in (mirroring Reading B), or drop the note block straight down from the marker with no dogleg and move it clear of the baseline label's vertical band.

**3. The zero datum is the least-marked point on the axis.** The zone edges at ±3% carry full-height mint extension lines; zero carries an ordinary 0.09in tick identical to every other even tick (`for (let p = -7; p <= 7; p += 1)`). On a drawing whose stated composition is "centred on the baseline," the baseline is invisible. Fix: draw a proper drafting centreline at x=ZERO — long-short dashed, mint, running from above the zone top through the axis. Genre-native, and it fixes the read in one object.

**4. The axis labels the only two values the narrative never mentions, and the zone is undimensioned.** Labelled values are −4%, 0, +4%. The narrative's numbers are −6.0, ±3.0, −2.0, 0. Nothing on the sheet tells you the zone edges are at ±3.0% — you have to count ticks. Compounding it, the gold arrow spans the *full* 6.0%-wide zone while its label reads `TYPICAL ERROR ± 3.0 %`. A full-span dimension labelled with a half-span value is exactly the ambiguity a sport scientist in this room catches by name ("is the band three or six?"). Treat these as one fix: label the zone edges −3.0% / +3.0% on the axis, keep 0, drop ±4%; and either split the gold dimension into two 3.0% dimensions from the zero centreline, or keep the single arrow and label it `6.0 % TOTAL · ± 3.0 % TYPICAL ERROR`.

**5. STORY beat 3 is carried by a 6.5pt abbreviation.** See CONTRACT AUDIT. Fix: replace `adj.` with `THRESHOLD — SET BY COST, NOT BY THE DATA` at ~9–10pt on one side (the second is a mirror and needs no repeat label), and pull the notes-column heading "The dashed line — adj." into plain language.

**6. The hatch is 2.15:1 against the forest ground at 0.6pt and will wash out under projection.** Measured: `MID_GREEN #1E6349` on `#0B2A1F` = 2.15:1. It reads on a 1500px screen render; it will not read on a projector with ambient light, and the hatched zone is the subject of the slide. Mitigation already present and working: the zone has mint boundaries on three sides (top rule plus both extension lines, 9.38:1), so the region survives even if the texture vanishes — this is why it is finding 6 and not finding 1. Fix: draw the hatch in `C.MINT` at 0.5pt with `step` widened from 0.115 to ~0.16 — fewer, brighter lines read as texture rather than as a fill, stay within palette, and preserve the refusal of the shaded band. (A mid-green fill under the hatch is the alternative, but it re-introduces the band.)

**7. Five names for one thing.** The sheet calls the same object "typical error", "tolerance", "the hatched zone", "the floor", and — in the title block claim — "the noise floor". Three of those appear within four inches of each other. For a room of peers this reads as imprecision rather than richness, and it forces the listener to re-map the vocabulary mid-slide. Fix: "typical error" on the dimension, "noise floor" in the claim and prose, retire "tolerance", "the hatched zone", and "the floor" as nouns.

**8. Three competing grids on a sheet whose whole authority is that it is drawn to a grid.** Frame at x 0.30/9.70; general-notes rule and columns at 0.46 / 3.58 / 6.70 spanning 0.46–9.54; title-block dividers at 5.55 / 7.70. Nothing in the lower third aligns with anything above it, and the notes rule starts 0.16in inboard of the frame rule directly below it, producing a visible jog. This is the own-world's one self-inflicted wound: a blueprint that does not keep its own grid. Fix: run the notes rule to the frame edges (0.30/9.70) and set the three note columns on the title-block divisions (0.46 / 5.71 / 7.86) so the foot of the sheet reads as one structure.

**Gold accent count:** the dimension is 4 shapes (rule, two arrowheads, label) against a cap written as "2 objects on one slide." Read as visual accents it is compliant — a drafting dimension is one object, and any shape-count reading would make every dimension illegal. It reads as a single gold element in the render. One recommendation only: have the department record the group interpretation in the design system, so the next build is not litigating it.

TRUTH CHECK

**The dashed threshold at ±4.5% is the strongest exposure.** It is unsourced, unlabelled, and precisely placed on a labelled axis, immediately outside the ±4% tick. The room will read a number off it. Nothing in Rebelo et al. or the brief supports 4.5%. Fix: either place it at the paper's own example (±1 SD, labelled as that example and as one setting among others), or move it to a deliberately non-committal position and label it as adjustable in words rather than in `adj.`

**`TYPICAL ERROR ± 3.0 %` stacked directly over `COEFFICIENT OF VARIATION OF THE PROTOCOL · ICC 0.96` asserts an equivalence the incumbent only implied.** The old band label was just "typical error of the test"; the new layout typesets CV as the definition of typical error. They are related but not the same quantity, and this room contains people who will say so. Fix: subtitle to `CV 3.0 % OF THE PROTOCOL · ICC 0.96 · REBELO ET AL. 2026` and let "typical error" stand as the drawing's working word without an equals sign.

**The illustrative labelling is present but underpowered — not missing.** Note 1 correctly says "Readings shown are illustrative", but at 7pt, in the bottom-left, roughly 1.5in from readings titled `READING B −6.0 %` and `READING A −2.0 %` at 9pt. The precise-looking numbers are three times the size of the disclaimer and nearer the eye. Fix: carry `(ILLUSTRATIVE)` in the reading callouts themselves, or a single `ILLUSTRATIVE READINGS` label ruled across the readings row.

**"Nothing has been observed yet"** is inherited from the deck's own language (`data-to-decision.js`, problem-slide notes) and is not a new overstatement here. Strictly it is "not distinguishable from measurement noise" rather than "nothing observed", but that is a deck-level wording question, not a render defect. Low priority.

**`REV A`** in the header is fabricated metadata on a sheet that otherwise carries real sourced numbers. Harmless costume, but it is the one element pretending to be a record. Minor — drop it or keep `SHEET 3 OF 5` alone.

**Note 3 is correct and well-judged:** "± 1 SD appears in the paper as one example of a sensitive setting, not as a standard." That is precisely the right caveat, in the right words. The source line in the notes column (Rebelo et al., Sports Medicine 2026 — CV 3.0 %, ICC 0.96) is likewise correct.

Content fidelity against `data-to-decision.js` `insight`: nothing meaningful was dropped. The head, both band captions, the two-ways-to-be-wrong argument, and the ±1 SD caveat all survive; the foot's "which mistake costs more is what should set your threshold" clause is relocated to the notes column ("The threshold is set by which of the two errors costs more here. Not by the statistic.") and reads better there.

WHAT NOT TO CHANGE

- **The signed −7…+7% axis.** This is a real improvement on the incumbent's one-sided "larger change →" magnitude axis: it matches what a dashboard actually shows a coach. Keep it even while fixing the tick labels.
- **The zone-drawn-from-data versus threshold-drawn-dashed distinction.** This is the slide's intellectual core and it is working. One line is measured, one line is chosen, and the drawing says so before any words do. Fix how it is labelled; do not fix the device.
- **The three-sided mint boundary on the zone.** It is what makes the zone survive a washed-out hatch. Do not remove it when the hatch is retuned.
- **Gold spent once, on the dimension.** Correct call, correct object.
- **The title block carrying the claim bottom-left.** Genre-native and it works; the fix is to raise its size, not to move it back to the top.
- **The leader-and-callout system.** The device is right and reads well for Reading B. Fix Reading A's routing only.
- **Note 3's wording, and the notes-column source line.** Both exactly right.
- **The refusal of the caption-inside-the-band default.** That refusal is what makes this not a re-skin, and it is the answer to the user's "they all look the same."

Axis labels −7 / 0 / +7 label the scale ends and the datum; the zone is dimensioned by the gold callout rather than by tick-counting, which is the drafting-correct answer. |
| 5 | STORY beat 3 on a 6.5pt abbreviation | **partial** | `adj.` gone, replaced by "THRESHOLD / Shown at an arbitrary position. Set by cost, not read off this axis." — plain language, correct content. But the body is 8pt in a 1.16in column, the smallest running copy on the sheet, and it is the sole in-drawing carrier of the beat. Raise to 9.5pt and widen the column. |
| 6 | Hatch washout at 2.15:1 | **resolved** | Hatch now MINT at 9.38:1, 0.5pt, 0.18in step; zone boundary raised to MINT_SOFT so the three-sided frame holds independently. Survives a lit room. (See new issue B.) |
| 7 | Five names for one thing | **resolved** | Visible text now uses exactly two: "typical error" for the measured quantity, "noise floor" for the idea. "Tolerance", "hatched zone", "the floor" are gone from the sheet. |

| Item | Status | Why |
|---|---|---|
| ±4.5% threshold unsourced | **resolved** | Says its own position is arbitrary, in words, at the line; Note 2 repeats it. No number is asserted. |
| CV / typical-error equivalence | **resolved** | "TYPICAL ERROR" over "CV 3.0 % OF THE PROTOCOL · ICC 0.96" now attributes a source rather than defining one term as the other. |

**A. The datum and the threshold are now both dashed MINT_SOFT verticals.** The centreline (long-short, 0.17/0.05) and the threshold lines (uniform 0.075/0.13) share colour, weight and hairline width — the measured/chosen distinction that is the slide's intellectual core now rests on dash rhythm alone, which does not survive projector distance.
